column1: # open-agent-robot — every ROS 2 topic in this tree with only one end wired.
# `infra/ros_census.py` derives two asymmetries from the source: a topic that is
# published and nobody subscribes to (a message written to nobody), and a topic that is
# subscribed and nobody publishes (a node waiting for what cannot arrive). Today there
# are four. There were seven when this manifest was written — five more than
# `docs/architecture.svg` drew before it existed, which is the argument for deriving the
# list instead of remembering it — and R1.1 then R1.2 wired three of them away.
# **All four remaining rows are `dead_end`, so the `orphan` direction is now empty.** That
# is a result and not a policy, and the difference matters: `unused` below is declared as a
# class that *should* stay empty, whereas `orphan` merely happens to have no members since
# R1.2 deleted `/memory/rps_table`. Nothing prevents the next one, and the census does not
# treat an empty direction as an achievement — it derives both directions every run. What
# an empty direction did break is a test that anchored a mutant to it; see
# `GAP_MUTANTS["asymmetry_direction_flipped"]` in `tests/test_architecture.py`, which
# raised KeyError rather than going red on the day the last `orphan` row was correctly
# deleted. A mutant pinned to a row is pinned to that row's continued existence.
# The asymmetry itself is machine-derived. Whether a given asymmetry is *acceptable* is
# a judgement, so it is a reviewable line with a stated reason — the same shape as
# `infra/standalone_entrypoints.tsv` and `infra/generated_paths.tsv`, and for the same
# reason: an excuse living inside the guard is where the next unreviewed exemption gets
# added.
# `tests/test_architecture.py` checks the manifest in both directions. A censused
# asymmetry with no row is a finding (an undocumented dead end). A row whose topic is no
# longer asymmetric is also a finding — a stale row would silently excuse the next topic
# that arrives with the same name, and it is the row that must be deleted on the day the
# missing end gets wired, in the same PR that wires it.
# `class` is a closed set, checked by the test:
#   external    the missing end is deliberately outside this repo (ROS tooling, a
#               driver, another stack). Nothing here will ever subscribe.
#   pending     the missing end belongs to a stage that has not landed. The row names
#               the stage, and the row is deleted when the stage lands.
#   defect      the edge is wrong as drawn, and the fix is known and written down.
#   unused      published as an observable signal with no consumer designed yet. This
#               class is the one that should stay empty over time: either something
#               needs the signal, or the publisher should go.
# Columns (tab-separated):  topic <TAB> asymmetry <TAB> class <TAB> reason
/detections_msg
column4: vision_msgs/Detection2DArray in the standard ROS 2 shape, published for consumers outside this repo (rviz2, another perception stack). Nothing here is meant to read it: the in-repo path is the throttled /detections string that agent_node subscribes to, and detect_node's docstring names both

column1: /joint_states
column4: body_node publishes it at the render tick, which round 6 found is the wrong direction — by ROS convention /joint_states is the driver's feedback topic, so on real hardware this collides with the G1 driver publishing the same name. The fix is to publish /joint_commands and leave /joint_states to the backend. See docs/research-round6-simreal-joint-mapping-2026-08-22.md §6 and README.md, which now states the defect in the place it used to state the seam as a feature

column1: /game/events
column4: ws_gateway publishes everything arriving from the MacBook side here: browser JSON events (frame type 0x10) and the daemon up/down lifecycle. No node subscribes, so a click on the face reaches the bus and stops there — voice is the wired path. The consumer is game_node, which today accepts commands only on /game/cmd from agent_node. Art 50(1) does not depend on this topic: ws_gateway speaks the disclosure directly on /speech/say, which is why it still works

column1: /speech/tts_done
column4: tts_node announces the id of a finished utterance. Nothing consumes it and nothing is designed to: the half-duplex gate uses /speech/tts_active, the Art 50(2) synthetic marking rides /speech/tts_started, and the segmenter's activity-transition rule reads /game/events_out. It is a published signal looking for a reason to exist
